and the penalty exposure $(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ disappear. This is the
reversal of the folk belief: leniency is strictly optimal for every
$\theta<1$ and the preference gap is eroded to zero as $\theta\uparrow1$,
with $x^{*}\equiv0$ on the interior and $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent. ∎

9.text:
Up to the $x$ free tax the relevant part of the expected outlay is
$$
\widetilde C(\theta ,x)=C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)
      =h(\theta)g(x),\qquad 
h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0 ,\;g(x)=xp(x), 
$$
$h(1)=0$ and, $F>0$ decreasing,
$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$
on the two point lattice
$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta),\qquad p_{1}=p(1)>0,
$$
$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p_{1}h(\theta)
      =p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)\ge0 .
$$
Hence
$$
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff h(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,\qquad\Delta(1)=0,
$$
$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff0\le\theta<1,\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$
and
$$
\Delta(\theta_{2})<\Delta(\theta_{1}),\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
\qquad
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=h'(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0,
$$
so $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$ and
$\partial_{x}C$ is decreasing in $\theta$. The incremental expected
penalty of a strict audit
$S(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ is strictly
decreasing in truthfulness and $S(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.

For $\theta<1$ the positive scalar $h(\theta)>0$ cancels in the $x$
ordering,
$$
\arg\min_{x}C(\theta ,x)=\arg\min_{x}h(\theta)g(x)
                       =\arg\min_{x}g(x),
$$
and with the normalisation $g(0)=0<g(1)$
$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$
with $C(1,x)\equiv t(1)$, i.e. $x^{*}(1)$ is payoff indifferent. With the
usual tie break $x^{*}(1)=0$
$$
x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0\quad{\rm on}\;[0,1),
$$
so that in the Milgrom–Shannon sense the weak best reply is 
weakly non-decreasing,
$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow
C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)\le C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0),
\qquad x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1}),
$$
i.e. a more truthful type finds a strict auditor relatively cheaper.
On the binary support the best reply is flat on the interior and
$$
C_{\theta x}<0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}h'(\theta)<0 .
$$

In strict monotone terms $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for
$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ never occurs on $(0,1)$; the strict
$\theta\uparrow\Rightarrow x^{*}\downarrow$ comparative static is vacuous
and the strict decreasing locus is empty, $x^{*}\equiv0$ on the interior.
Up to the harmless knife edge indifference $h(1)=0$ the lenient audit
$x=0$ is the unique strict minimiser for every non-perfect type,
$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
$$
the weak dominance $C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ holding on the whole
support with strict dominance $0\le\theta<1$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the
perfectly truthful limit where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$
vanishes. This is the usual flat limiting case of the positive sorting
$x^{*}\!\uparrow\!\theta$ and the reversal of the folk belief: the
preference for leniency is strongest for low types and is eroded to
indifference only as $\theta\uparrow1$. With the conventional tie break
the optimum can be written $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1]$, the strict
preference for $x=0$ being $0\le\theta<1$ and empty in the strict
monotone $x^{*}\downarrow\theta$ sense. ∎

10.text:
Up to the $x$ free tax $t(\theta )$ the $x$ marginal part of the
expected outlay is
$$
\widetilde C(\theta ,x)=C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=x(1-\theta )p(x)F(\theta)
      =h(\theta )g(x),\qquad 
h(\theta )=(1-\theta )F(\theta)>0,\;\;g(x)=xp(x),
$$
$h(1)=0$ and, $F>0$ decreasing,

$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta )F'(\theta)<0\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$
in the discrete sense.  On $\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta),\;p_{1}=p(1)>0,
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)
      =p_{1}h(\theta)=p_{1}(1-\theta )F(\theta)\ge0,
$$
and

$$
\Delta'(\theta)=p_{1}h'(\theta)<0,\qquad 
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff h(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,\qquad \Delta(1)=0 .
$$

Hence
$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\qquad 
C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$
and in differential form

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=h(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]>0,\qquad
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=h'(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0,
\qquad\theta<1,
$$
i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.  The
incremental expected penalty of a strict audit

$$
S(\theta)=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0
$$
is strictly decreasing in truthfulness and $S(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$.  For $\theta<1$ the positive scalar $h(\theta)>0$
cancels out of the $x$-ordering,
$\arg\min_{x}C(\theta ,x)=\arg\min_{x}g(x)$, and with the normalisation
$g(0)=0<g(1)$

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$
with $C(1,x)\equiv t(1)$ so that $x^{*}(1)$ is payoff indifferent.
In particular the weak best reply is weakly non-decreasing in
$\theta$,

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow 
C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)\le C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0),\qquad
x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1}),
$$

i.e. a more truthful type finds a stricter auditor relatively cheaper.
On the binary support the best reply is flat on the whole
non-degenerate type space,
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$, the usual tie
break being $x^{*}(1)=0$.

Hence in the strict monotone sense
$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Rightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$
never occurs on $(0,1)$; the strict $x^{*}\!\downarrow\!\theta$
comparative static is vacuous and the strict decreasing locus is empty.
Up to the harmless degenerate indifference at the top the weak
dominance of the lenient audit is
$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
$$
the unique strict optimum being $x=0$ for every non perfect type
$0\le\theta<1$ and indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the knife edge
$\theta=1$ where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.
Neglecting the zero measure indifference this is the conventional
dominance region $0\le\theta<1$, i.e. $\theta<1$, of the lenient
auditor.  This is the limit of the usual positive sorting
$x^{*}\!\uparrow\!\theta$: the refusal risk $x(1-\theta)$ makes a
strict, reputation-building auditor strictly costly for every
$\theta<1$, with the cost gap $\Delta(\theta)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$
positive and strictly decreasing to zero as $\theta\uparrow1$. ∎

5.text:
Up to the $\theta$ free tax the $x$–marginal part of the expected outlay is

\begin{equation*}
\widetilde C(\theta ,x)=C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)
          =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)=h(\theta)g(x),\qquad 
h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,\;g(x)=xp(x),
\end{equation*}
$h(1)=0$.  On the two point lattice

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta),\qquad p_{1}=p(1)>0 ,
\end{equation*}
so that with $t(\theta)$ stripped off

\begin{equation*}
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p_{1}h(\theta)
      =p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)\ge0,
\end{equation*}
is the extra expected second stage cost of a strict audit.  $F>0$ is
decreasing and $1-\theta$ is decreasing, hence in the discrete sense

\begin{equation*}
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
\end{equation*}
$h(1)=0$ and $h(\theta)>0$ for $\theta<1$.  In particular

\begin{equation*}
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff h(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,\qquad 
\Delta(1)=0,
\end{equation*}
and

\begin{equation*}
\Delta(\theta_{2})<\Delta(\theta_{1}),\qquad 
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}<1,
\end{equation*}
i.e.

\begin{equation*}
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=h'(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0,\qquad 
\theta<1,
\end{equation*}
so $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$ and
$\partial_{\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}h'(\theta)<0$.
Hence

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1),\qquad0\le\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
\end{equation*}
and the incremental expected penalty of strictness
$S(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0$ is strictly decreasing in
truthfulness and $S(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.
For $\theta<1$ the positive scalar $h(\theta)$ cancels in the $x$
ordering,

\begin{equation*}
\arg\min_{x}C(\theta ,x)=\arg\min_{x}g(x)=\arg\min_{x}xp(x),
\end{equation*}
and with the normalisation $g(0)=0<g(1)$

\begin{equation*}
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
\end{equation*}
$C(1,x)\equiv t(1)$ so $x^{*}(1)$ is payoff indifferent.  With the
usual tie break $x^{*}(1)=0$

\begin{equation*}
x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0\;\;{\rm on}\;[0,1), \qquad 
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=h(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0,\;\theta<1,
\end{equation*}
i.e. the best reply is flat on the non-degenerate part of the type
space.  In Milgrom-Shannon/Topkis terms $C_{\theta x}<0$ gives the weak
order

\begin{equation*}
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge
x^{*}(\theta_{1}),\qquad 
C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)\le C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0),
\end{equation*}
so a more truthful type finds a stricter auditor relatively cheaper.
The strict monotone move $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Rightarrow
x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ has empty interior; the strict
$x^{*}\!\downarrow\!\theta$ locus is vacuous and $x^{*}$ is constant $0$
on $[0,1)$.  Up to the harmless boundary indifference this is the
conventional weak dominance of leniency

\[
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\]

i.e. $x=0$ is the unique strict minimiser for every non-perfect type
$0\le\theta<1$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the knife edge where the refusal
probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.  In the usual operational
statement this is quoted as the interior dominance region
$0\le\theta<1$, with indifference only at the degenerate top
$\theta=1$.  This is the reversal of the folk belief: the refusal risk
$x(1-\theta)$ makes a strict reputable audit strictly costly for every
$\theta<1$, the cost gap $\Delta(\theta)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ being
positive and strictly decreasing to zero as $\theta\to1$. ∎

\widetilde C(\theta ,x)=C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)
       =h(\theta)g(x),\qquad 
h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,\;\;g(x)=xp(x),
$$

and on the $0\!-\!1$ lattice

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta),\;p_{1}=p(1)>0,
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p_{1}h(\theta)
      =p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)\ge 0 .
$$

$F>0$ decreasing and $1-\theta$ decreasing give in the discrete sense

$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,\qquad h(1)=0,
$$

so that $h$ and $\Delta$ are strictly decreasing on $[0,1)$ and

$$
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff h(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,\qquad\Delta(1)=0,
$$

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff0\le\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

with

$$
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=h'(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0,\qquad\theta<1,
$$

i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$ and 
$\partial_{\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}h'(\theta)<0$.
The incremental expected second stage cost of a strict audit

$$
S(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0
$$

is strictly decreasing in truthfulness and $S(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$ where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.

For $\theta<1$ the positive scalar $h(\theta)>0$ cancels in the $x$ ordering,
$\arg\min_{x}C(\theta ,x)=\arg\min_{x}g(x)$, and with the normalisation
$g(0)=0<g(1)$

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

$C(1,x)\equiv t(1)$ and with the usual tie break $x^{*}(1)=0$.
Hence the best reply is flat on the interior,

$$
x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0\quad{\rm on}\;[0,1),
$$

and in the Milgrom–Shannon sense it is weakly non-decreasing,
$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Rightarrow C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)
\le C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0)$, i.e. a more truthful type finds a
strict auditor relatively cheaper.

In strict monotone terms 
$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Rightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$
never occurs on $(0,1)$; the strict $\theta\uparrow\Rightarrow x^{*}\downarrow$
locus is empty. Up to the harmless knife edge indifference the weak
dominance of leniency is

$$
C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)\;\forall\theta,\qquad 
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
$$

the unique strict optimum being $x=0$ for every non-perfect type 
$0\le\theta<1$ with $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the perfect truthful limit.
Conventionally this is quoted as the interior dominance region
$0\le\theta<1$, $\Delta(\theta)>0$, the degenerate indifference
$\Delta(1)=0$ being the limit in which the refusal risk $x(1-\theta)$
and the penalty exposure $(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ disappear. This is the
reversal of the folk belief: leniency is strictly optimal for every
$\theta<1$ and the preference gap is eroded to zero as $\theta\uparrow1$,
with $x^{*}\equiv0$ on the interior and $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent. ∎

Up to the $x$ free tax $t(\theta)$ the $x$ marginal cost is

$$
\widetilde C(\theta ,x)=C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)
      =h(\theta)g(x),\qquad h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,\;
      g(x)=xp(x),
$$

$h(1)=0$ and with $F>0$ decreasing

$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

in the discrete sense.  On $\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta),\;p_{1}=p(1)>0,
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=p_{1}h(\theta)
      =p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)\ge0 ,
$$

and

$$
\partial_{\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}h'(\theta)<0,\qquad
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff h(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,\qquad\Delta(1)=0 .
$$

Hence

$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff0\le\theta<1,\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

and

$$
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=h'(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0,\qquad
\theta<1,
$$

so $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$,
$C_{x}(\theta ,x)=h(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0$ for $\theta<1$ and
$\partial_{x}C$ is decreasing in $\theta$.
The incremental expected second stage cost of a strict audit

$$
S(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0
$$

is strictly decreasing in truthfulness and $S(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$ where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.

For $\theta<1$ the positive scalar $h(\theta)>0$ cancels in the
$x$-ordering,

$$
\arg\min_{x}C(\theta ,x)=\arg\min_{x}h(\theta)g(x)=\arg\min_{x}g(x),
\qquad\theta<1,
$$

and with the normalisation $g(0)=0<g(1)$

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

$C(1,x)\equiv t(1)$ and with the usual tie break $x^{*}(1)=0$.
In Milgrom-Shannon/Topkis terms

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow
C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)\le C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0),
$$

so the weak best reply is weakly non-decreasing $x^{*}\!\uparrow\!\theta$
and a more truthful type finds a strict auditor relatively cheaper.
On the binary support the best reply is flat on the non-degenerate
type space

$$
x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0\ {\rm on}\ [0,1),
$$

the lenient auditor $x=0$ being the unique strict minimiser for every
non-perfect type.  In strict monotone terms

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never occurs on $(0,1)$; the strict $\theta\uparrow\Rightarrow
x^{*}\!\downarrow$ comparative static is vacuous and the strict
decreasing locus is empty.  Up to the harmless knife edge indifference
the weak dominance of leniency is the interior dominance

$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
$$

conventionally quoted as $0\le\theta<1$, with $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ the
degenerate limit where $h(1)=0$ and the refusal risk $x(1-\theta)$
disappears.  This is the reversal of the folk belief: the preference
for $x=0$ is strongest for low $\theta$ and is eroded monotonically to
indifference as $\theta\uparrow1$, with the cost gap
$\Delta(\theta)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ positive and strictly
decreasing to zero at the top.  With the conventional tie break

On the $x$ free part

$$
\widetilde C(\theta ,x)=C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)
      =h(\theta)g(x) ,\qquad h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0 ,
\;g(x)=xp(x),
$$

and on $\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta),\qquad p_{1}=p(1)>0,
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p_{1}h(\theta)
      =p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)\ge0 .
$$

$F>0$ decreasing gives in the discrete sense

$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,\qquad h(1)=0,
$$

so $h$ and $\Delta$ are strictly decreasing on $[0,1)$ and

$$
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff h(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1 ,\qquad 
\Delta(1)=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff0\le\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1)
$$

and

$$
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=h'(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0,\qquad\theta<1,
$$

so $C$ has decreasing differences.  The incremental expected second
stage cost of a strict audit

$$
S(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0
$$

is strictly decreasing in truthfulness and $S(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$.  For $\theta<1$ the positive scalar $h(\theta)>0$
cancels in the $x$-ordering,

$$
\arg\min_{x}C(\theta ,x)=\arg\min_{x}h(\theta)g(x)=\arg\min_{x}g(x),
$$

and with $g(0)=0<g(1)$

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

$C(1,x)\equiv t(1)$ and with the usual tie break $x^{*}(1)=0$.  Hence
in the Milgrom–Shannon/Topkis sense

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow 
C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)\le C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0),
\qquad x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1}),

and the weak best reply is weakly non-decreasing.  On the binary
support the best reply is flat on the non-degenerate part of the type
space,

$$

$$

so that in strict monotone terms

$$

$$

never occurs on $(0,1)$.  The strict $\theta\uparrow\Rightarrow
x^{*}\downarrow$ comparative static is vacuous and the strict
decreasing locus is empty.

dominance of leniency

$$
